phases.name: Walking Skeleton — Devon's second launch shows yesterday's inventory instantly from cache
phases.description: Thinnest end-to-end vertical slice that proves the SQLite cache wiring works: a new `modeltap-store` crate (Cache::open + migrate v0->v1 + minimal ToolsRepo/ModelsRepo write+read paths), the two new `Tool::inspect_tool` / `Tool::inspect_model` default-body methods in `modeltap-core`, an in-process `TestTool` plugin registered via `MODELTAP_TEST_PLUGINS=test-tool`, and the `modeltap-app::orchestration::warm_start` composition glue that reads the cache on launch and paints from it. Exit gate is the M1 @walking-skeleton scenario in `walking-skeleton.feature` passing end-to-end: process A cold-starts, writes one row to a real on-disk `cache.sqlite`, exits cleanly; process B launches against the same file, paints the row from cache, and reports `launch.warm_paint_ms <= 150` in JSONL. Closes the four riskiest assumptions at once: (a) the trait extension is source-compatible across all 6 plugins, (b) rusqlite_migration runs v0->v1 cleanly, (c) the WAL/busy_timeout PRAGMAs persist across process boundaries, (d) the `modeltap-store` adapter is wired correctly into `modeltap-app`'s composition root. Litmus test (acceptance-test-plan.md §4): deleting the real `modeltap-store` adapter and substituting an `InMemoryCache` would break the walking skeleton because process B has no in-memory state. Confirmed Strategy B (real I/O against fixture-populated tempdirs).
